expectations.text: The response opens with a one- or two-sentence summary of what the message means before any detail
expectations.evidence: Opens with a one-line gist in Vercel's voice: 'I'm ready... but the internet doesn't know to send people to me yet.'

expectations.text: The response includes an everyday analogy that says which real-world thing stands for which technical part (for example the domain, the record and the server)
expectations.evidence: Says DNS 'works like a phone book' but maps only that one part; the domain, the record and Vercel aren't mapped to anything.

expectations.text: Every technical term or acronym the response uses (DNS, CNAME, TTL, SSL) is either explained in everyday words the first time or not used at all
expectations.evidence: CNAME is used as a field value with no explanation; TTL is mentioned ('leave it on whatever the default is') without saying what it is.

expectations.text: The response gives concrete next steps Sam can follow, including adding the record with name demo and value cname.vercel-dns.com
expectations.evidence: Step 4 gives Type CNAME, Name demo, Value cname.vercel-dns.com.

expectations.text: The response says the change can take time (up to 48 hours) to take effect, in plain words
expectations.evidence: 'Vercel says "up to 48 hours" to cover itself, but it's rarely that long.'
